facts.statement: Albertadromeus is an extinct thescelosaurid dinosaur found in the Late Cretaceous Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Albertadromeus is an extinct genus of orodromine thescelosaurid dinosaur known from the upper part of the Late Cretaceous Oldman Formation (middle Campanian stage) of Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: Albertadromeus was described and named by Caleb Marshall Brown, David C. Evans, Michael J. Ryan, and Anthony P. Russell in 2013.
facts.quote: This dinosaur was described and named by Caleb Marshall Brown, David C. Evans, Michael J. Ryan & Anthony P. Russell in 2013

facts.statement: The genus name Albertadromeus means "runner from Alberta", referencing its inferred ability to run.
facts.quote: The composite term Albertadromeus is derived from the name of the Canadian province "Alberta", and the Greek word dromeus (δρομεύς) meaning "runner", a reference to its inferred cursorial nature

facts.statement: The species name syntarsus means "together-ankle", referring to the fusion of the distal fibula to the distal tibia.
facts.quote: The specific name, syntarsus is derived from Greek words "syn" (συν) meaning "together" and "tarsus" (ταρσός) meaning "ankle", hence "together-ankle" a reference to the condition where its distal fibula is fused to its distal tibia.

facts.statement: Albertadromeus was a small, bipedal, herbivorous dinosaur built for running.
facts.quote: Albertadromeus was a small-bodied, bipedal, cursorially adapted (built to run) neornithischian.

facts.statement: Albertadromeus is the smallest known herbivorous dinosaur in Canada, measuring about 1.6 meters long and weighing 16 kilograms.
facts.quote: It is the smallest known herbivore dinosaur in Canada being around 1.6 meters long and weighed 16 Kg (30 Ibs)

facts.statement: Albertadromeus had an elongated tibia that indicates it was adapted for running.
facts.quote: Its elongate tibia has been strongly correlated with cursorial habits.

facts.statement: Albertadromeus had a distal fibula reduced to a thin bone sheet fused to the front of the tibia for the distal third of its length.
facts.quote: The distal fibula is reduced to a thin sheet of bone that is fused to the anterior surface of tibia for the distal one-third of its length

facts.statement: Albertadromeus possessed a prominent cnemial crest on the tibia that projected upward and outward.
facts.quote: A prominent cnemial crest that projects dorsally (and anterolaterally), resulting in a posterior sloped dorsal extremity of the tibia

facts.statement: Researchers created the subfamily Orodrominae to group species like Albertadromeus that are closely related to Orodromeus.
facts.quote: Brown et al. (2013) erected a new taxon Orodrominae to differentiate those species that are more closely related to Orodromeus from those more closely related to Thescelosaurus.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests Albertadromeus is closely related to Zephyrosaurus and Orodromeus.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses suggest that Albertadromeus forms a clade with Zephyrosaurus and Orodromeus, with Oryctodromeus being less closely related.

facts.statement: Albertadromeus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 77 to 76 million years ago.
facts.quote: The specimen was collected in a two-meter-thick fine to very fine sandstone unit that was deposited during the Campanian stage of the Cretaceous period, approximately 77 to 76 million years ago.

facts.statement: Albertadromeus lived in an ancient coastal plain environment.
facts.quote: Studies suggest that the paleoenvironment of the Oldman Formation was an ancient coastal plain.

facts.statement: Albertadromeus was a herbivore that likely specialized in eating ferns and low vegetation.
facts.quote: It is considered a herbivore, probably specialised in the consumption of: ferns and low vegetation.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Albertadromeus is housed in the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology in Drumheller, Alberta.
facts.quote: Este ejemplar, TMP 2009.037.0044, se encuentra en la colección del Museo Tyrrell en Drumheller, Alberta.

facts.statement: The tibia of Albertadromeus is slightly longer than that of Orodromeus and significantly longer than those of Parksosaurus, Thescelosaurus, Hypsilophodon, Dryosaurus, and Stegoceras.
facts.quote: La tibia de Albertadromeus es algo más alargada que la de Orodromeus, y bastante más que la de Parksosaurus, ROM 804, Thescelosaurus, USNM 7757 y RSM P 1225.1, Hypsilophodon, NMHUK R5830, Dryosaurus y Stegoceras, UALVP 002.

facts.statement: Albertadromeus belongs to the subfamily Orodrominae, which also includes Zephyrosaurus, Orodromeus, and Oryctodromeus.
facts.quote: Orodrominae incluye a Albertadromeus, Zephyrosaurus, Orodromeus y Oryctodromeus.

facts.statement: Albertadromeus is classified within the family Thescelosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Thescelosauridae

facts.statement: Albertadromeus is classified as a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Albertadromeus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Studies suggest the paleoenvironment of the Oldman Formation, where Albertadromeus fossils were found, was an ancient coastal plain.
facts.quote: Los estudios sugieren que el paleoambiente de la Formación Oldman era una antigua planicie costera.

facts.statement: The Oldman Formation contained fossils of various dinosaurs that shared the same environment with Albertadromeus, including theropods like Saurornitholestes and Daspletosaurus, ceratopsians like Albertaceratops and Chasmosaurus, and hadrosaurids like Brachylophosaurus and Parasaurolophus.
facts.quote: Esta formación ha producido los restos de los terópodos Saurornitholestes, Daspletosaurus, Troodon y Dromaeosaurus, los ceratópsidos Albertaceratops, Chasmosaurus, Anchiceratops, y Coronosaurus, los hadrosáuridos Brachylophosaurus, Gryposaurus, Parasaurolophus y Corythosaurus, así como otros dinosaurios que compartían que su paleoambiente con Albertadromeus.
